To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
pellagra is a disease that is caused by a lack of vitamin B3, also called niacin.
pellagra is caused by a deficiency in niacin (nicotine acid) and/or in its tryptophane (Trp)precursor, which is compounded by B vitamins deficiencies.

Pellagra is caused mainly by niacin and/or its trytpophan precursor deficiency, aggravated by B vitamin deficiencies, and is induced or aggravated by drugs inhibiting conversion of Trp into niacin and by gastrointestinal dysfunction.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the biochemical mechanisms by which niacin deficiency and its tryptophane (Trp) and B vitamin precursors and co-factors cause the skin and neurological symptoms of pellagra, and how these biochemical mechanisms are affected by alcoholism.
the elucidation of the biochemical basis of pellagra, and the application of this knowledge to the understanding of the biochemical basis for alcohol-induced pellagra.
elucidating the role of Trp metabolites in the pathogenesis of pellagra.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
pellagra and alcohol are both bad for your health.
pellagra and alcohol are closely linked and should be considered together.

the pellagra-like symptoms in alcoholics may be due to the combined effects of niacin deficiency, B vitamin deficiencies, gastrointestinal dysfunction, Trp deficiency, 5-ALA excess and porphyrin excess.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pellagra is caused by the deficiency of niacin and/or its precursor, Trp, and that the clinical manifestations are caused by the deficiency and accumulation of the Trp and its metabolites.
the biochemical and clinical features of pellagra are due to the interplay of niacin, Trp, 5-ALA, porphyrins, zinc and B vitamin deficiencies.
pellagra and alcohol abuse share a common pathogenesis and that the biochemical abnormalities in pellagra are aggravated by alcohol abuse.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pellagra is not just a nutritional deficiency disease.
alcohol abuse can induce or aggravation pellagra and that the symptoms of pellagra can be managed with niacine and other B vitamin supplements and adequate protein nutrition.
pellagra should be considered as a potential cause of neurological disturbances in alcoholism and treated appropriately with niacin and other B vitamins.
